title: AWS WAF and Shield (perimeter hardening)
hook: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) filters HTTP and HTTPS requests using managed and custom rules at the edge. AWS Shield Standard protects all customers from common network-layer DDoS at no charge; Shield Advanced adds cost protection, 24/7 DDoS Response Team access, and deeper visibility.

blocks.text: AWS WAF attaches to Amazon CloudFront distributions, Application Load Balancers, API Gateway REST APIs, AppSync, and Cognito user pools. Rules match IP sets, geographic locations, rate limits, SQL injection, or AWS Managed Rules groups. Shield Standard is automatic. Shield Advanced is a paid subscription with proactive engagement and financial protection for scaling costs during attacks.

entries.plainDefinition: Layer 7 rule engine allowing or blocking HTTP requests before they reach your origin.
Container for ordered WAF rules with default allow or block action.
Always-on network/transport DDoS protection for AWS resources at no extra cost.
entries.example: Automatic SYN flood mitigation on CloudFront.

entries.plainDefinition: Paid DDoS protection with DRT support, cost protection, and advanced metrics.
entries.example: Enterprise e-commerce during holiday traffic spikes.

blocks.text: Application-layer attacks bypass network firewalls — SQL injection, credential stuffing, and bot scrapers hit HTTP paths. WAF is the AWS-native answer at CloudFront and ALB. Shield Advanced is the interview topic for financial protection when Auto Scaling spikes during DDoS. Know which resources WAF attaches to and rule evaluation order.

blocks.title: Defense in depth
blocks.body: Shield (L3/L4) + WAF (L7) + security groups (ENI) — each layer catches different attack types.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — WAF Web ACL with managed rules
snippet.code:
WebAcl:
  Type: AWS::WAFv2::WebACL
  Properties:
    Name: prod-acl
    Scope: CLOUDFRONT
    DefaultAction:
      Allow: {}
    Rules:
      - Name: AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet
        Priority: 1
        OverrideAction:
          None: {}
        Statement:
          ManagedRuleGroupStatement:
            VendorName: AWS
            Name: AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet
        VisibilityConfig:
          SampledRequestsEnabled: true
          CloudWatchMetricsEnabled: true
          MetricName: commonRules
snippet.explanation: CLOUDFRONT scope Web ACLs deploy to us-east-1. Managed rules need tuning exclusions for false positives.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — rate-based rule
snippet.code:
RateRule:
  Type: AWS::WAFv2::WebACL
  Properties:
    Scope: REGIONAL
    DefaultAction:
      Allow: {}
    Rules:
      - Name: RateLimitPerIp
        Priority: 0
        Action:
          Block: {}
        Statement:
          RateBasedStatement:
            Limit: 2000
            AggregateKeyType: IP
snippet.explanation: Regional scope for ALB/API Gateway. Blocks IPs exceeding 2000 requests per 5-minute window.

snippet.label: CLI — associate WAF with ALB
snippet.explanation: Regional WAF for ALB in the same Region. CloudFront uses CLOUDFRONT scope in us-east-1.

snippet.label: CLI — sampled blocked requests
snippet.code:
aws wafv2 get-sampled-requests \
  --web-acl-arn arn:aws:wafv2:us-east-1:123:regional/webacl/prod/abc \
  --rule-metric-name RateLimitPerIp \
  --scope REGIONAL \
  --time-window StartTime=1710000000,EndTime=1710003600 \
  --max-items 100
snippet.explanation: Debug false positives before blocking production traffic — tune exclusions on managed rules.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Regional WAF ACL on CloudFront — must use CLOUDFRONT scope in us-east-1. Managed rules with zero exclusions breaking JSON APIs. Relying on WAF alone without Shield awareness for volumetric attacks.

blocks.text: WAF rule capacity units (WCUs) limit rule complexity — consolidate rules or use rule groups. Shield Advanced protects ELB, CloudFront, Route53, Global Accelerator. How to prove it in production: CloudWatch BlockedRequests metric spikes during attack; enable WAF logging to S3/Kinesis; game day with controlled rate-based trigger; compare origin request count with CloudFront when WAF blocks at edge.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying Shield Advanced replaces WAF or security groups. Strong answer: Shield = DDoS (L3/L4); WAF = HTTP filter (L7); SG = ENI firewall — complementary layers.

interviewTakeaways: WAF = Layer 7 Web ACL rules on CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway REST, AppSync.
Shield Standard is free and automatic; Shield Advanced adds DRT and cost protection.
Managed rule groups need tuning exclusions for JSON APIs and webhooks.
60s: WAF filters HTTP at edge. Shield handles DDoS. Standard free; Advanced paid with DRT. Rule priority order matters. CLOUDFRONT scope in us-east-1.
Follow-up: how do rate-based rules affect users behind carrier-grade NAT?
commonPitfalls: Confusing WAF with security groups — rejected; WAF is HTTP edge, SG is ENI TCP/UDP.
Strong answer: WAF L7 + Shield DDoS + SG ENI — three layers, different scopes.
CLOUDFRONT Web ACL created in wrong Region — must be us-east-1.
Block default action with untested managed rules — production outage on first deploy.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Express helmet sets response headers at origin — WAF blocks malicious requests before they reach Node, reducing CPU on attack traffic.
TypeScript Stripe webhook HMAC validates payload at app layer — WAF still needed for volumetric junk hitting the same endpoint.
